specification.problem: Approximate a diagonal n-qubit unitary D=sum_x exp(i theta(x))|x><x| with only k distinct phase values using about k phase rotations (Clifford+T approximated) plus an entangling index-computation cost E(n,k), instead of 2^n rotations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance (assumed n=3, k=3 phases on 8 basis states, m=2 index ancillas). Construction: compute phase-index j(x) into an m-qubit register, apply the diagonal on the index register via parity Rz rotations, uncompute. Out of scope: the paper's actual E(n,k) optimization, the optimal decision boundary in (n,k,epsilon), the proof of the C0 bounds, and the comparison against other synthesis methods.

symbols.meaning: number of distinct phases in D
quality factor of the rotation synthesis method
entanglement cost of the index oracle, in T gates
index of the level set containing x

equations.label: Target diagonal
equations.description: D takes k distinct phase values determined by level sets of x.
equations.abstract_quote: $k$ is the number of distinct phases in the diagonal $n$-qubit unitary
equations.justification: Defines D from the abstract's k distinct phases; the level-set form is the sketch's construction.
assumptions: The partition is known classically at compile time

equations.label: Compute-phase-uncompute
equations.latex: D\otimes I_{anc}=U_j^{\dagger}\,(I_n\otimes \Delta)\,U_j,\quad U_j|x\rangle|0\rangle=|x\rangle|j(x)\rangle,\quad \Delta=\sum_{j<k}e^{i\phi_j}|j\rangle\langle j|+\text{(any phases on unused }j\ge k)
equations.description: Phase is written on the index register, then the index is uncomputed, returning ancillas to |0>.
equations.justification: Proposed construction from the sketch; the abstract only implies an entanglement cost.

equations.label: Parity (Walsh) decomposition of index diagonal
equations.description: The index diagonal is a product of Rz rotations on parities Z^s of index bits. Coefficients alpha_s come from the Walsh-Hadamard transform of phi_j. The sketch claims at most k-1 are needed.
equations.justification: Standard phase-polynomial/Walsh expansion. For k=2^m there are 2^m-1 nontrivial parities. The k-1 reduction for general k needs free phases on unused indices, which is an assumption.
assumptions: Unused index values may take free phases

equations.label: T-count bound
equations.description: Equivalent T-count bound of the synthesized circuit.
equations.abstract_quote: The equivalent $T$-count of the synthesized circuit is bounded by $kC_{0}\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)+E(n,k)$

equations.label: Per-rotation precision
equations.description: Linear error accumulation across k rotations. The log k term is dropped in the stated bound, which treats it as lower order.
equations.justification: Triangle inequality for operator-norm errors; the sketch says precision epsilon/k.

registers.name: data
registers.role: input qubits on which D acts

registers.name: toffoli_work
registers.role: optional extra ancillas for multi-controlled gate decomposition

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary data state (test on all basis states or the full unitary); index and work ancillas in |0>.

steps.description: Classically group the 2^n basis states into k level sets by phase and assign index j.
Build the reversible oracle U_j with CNOT/Toffoli/multi-controlled X gates, e.g. via ESOP or XOR-sum synthesis, writing j(x) into the index register.
Compute Walsh coefficients alpha_s of phi_j. For each parity s, CNOT the parity into one index qubit, apply Rz(alpha_s), and uncompute the CNOTs.
Optionally replace each Rz by a Clifford+T approximation at precision epsilon/k. For exact-rotation simulation, keep Rz.
Apply U_j^dagger to uncompute the index register, so the ancillas return to |0>.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the circuit's unitary or statevector, restricted to ancillas |0>, against D up to global phase (compare diag(D) after removing the phase of entry 0), with tolerance epsilon. Optionally count T gates against eq_4.
assumptions: Tiny instance n=3, k=3 is a choice, not from the abstract
Phases and level sets are known at compile time
Index has ceil(log2 k) qubits plus optional work qubits within the cap
Standard Rz Clifford+T synthesizer such as gridsynth
E(n,k) comes from a generic reversible synthesis, not an optimum
No measurements; the runner reads the unitary or statevector
